sum: Five days north-east of Pokhara: a rough ride to the Gurung village of Sikles, a day among its stone houses, then two forest days over Tara Hill Top at about 3,000 m to Ghalekharka.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. Here you need one in any case: the path over Tara Hill Top is unsigned, crosses forest with no settlements and may mean carrying food and a tent. Add someone from Sikles who has walked it this season.

access: Sikles is at the end of a rough road up the Madi Khola valley, three to four hours from Pokhara by jeep and longer by the local bus. The crossing comes out at Ghalekharka, two to three hours' walk above the nearest road, from where a jeep takes an hour or two to reach Pokhara. If you decide against the crossing, you simply ride back from Sikles.

photo.a: The blue-roofed houses of Sikles cover a sunlit spur among terraced fields, below forested slopes and a wall of snow-covered peaks.
photo.c: The Gurung village of Sikles, below the Annapurna range

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways
transportExtra: the jeep or bus from Pokhara to Sikles and the jeep back from below Ghalekharka
tips: Confirm in Sikles, not in Pokhara, whether the Tara Hill Top teahouse is open and stocked. Your homestay host will know.
Hire a local guide or porter in the village for the two forest days, even if you already have a guide from Pokhara.
Carry a sleeping bag, a head torch, water treatment and snacks for two days.
Bring cash from Pokhara. There is no cash machine in the valley.
Ask before you photograph people, and dress modestly. Sikles is a working village, and you are a guest in someone's house.

days.note: A rough road up the Madi Khola valley, dusty in the dry months and muddy after rain, with a steep last climb to the village. Jeeps take three to four hours and the local bus longer. Find your homestay, then walk up through the stone lanes before dark. At 1,980 m the evenings are cool even in spring.

n: Centre point maya gurung home stay

days.note: Spend the day on foot in the village: the stone lanes and courtyards, the conservation area office and the fields above the top houses, which look up the valley to Lamjung Himal and Annapurna II. Ask your hosts whether the teahouse on Tara Hill Top is open, and arrange a local guide or porter for the crossing.

n: Centre point maya gurung home stay

days.note: A climb of about 1,000 m on a narrow forest path through oak and rhododendron, with no village or tea shop on the way and no water you can count on. Carry lunch and two litres each. The top is a clearing on the ridge with one very basic teahouse; if it is shut, you camp. Be up at first light for the view.
why: A climb of 1,020 m in one day, to sleep at 3,000 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.note: Down the far side of the ridge: about 1,300 m of descent through forest and the cattle pasture of Nyauli Kharka, steep and slippery in places and hard on the knees. Side trails lead to herders' camps and nothing is signed, which is the main reason to take a local guide. Ghalekharka has homestay rooms and a campsite.

days.t: Walk out to the road, drive to Pokhara
days.note: Walk down to the nearest roadhead, two to three hours on village paths, and meet a jeep booked the day before for the ride of an hour or two to Pokhara. The roadhead moves as the track is extended, so let your guide or host fix the meeting point. The old trail carries on down to the Bhurjung Khola instead.
